title: Derived Hom groups from a constructible integral complex commute with countable bounded-below sums
statement:
Let $\ell$ be prime, $E/\mathbf Q_\ell$ finite, $A=\mathcal O_E$ and $\varpi$ a uniformizer [def-weil-l-adic-coefficient-extension]. Let $X$ be a noetherian finite-dimensional scheme on which $\ell$ is invertible [def-pc-scheme]; noetherian means a finite affine cover by spectra of noetherian rings, and finite-dimensional means a finite bound on lengths of strict chains of irreducible closed subsets. Write $A_Y(V)=C(|V|,A)$ and $E_Y(V)=C(|V|,E)$ on the small pro-etale site of any locally closed subscheme $Y$ of $X$ [def-weil-pbc-proetale-site]. Use sheaf modules [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category] and $S_Y(M)=E_Y\otimes_{A_Y}M$ [def-pur-sheaf-tensor-product]. Constructible integral means continuous-constructible as in [def-weil-pbc-continuous-constructible-module], with local models $A_Y\otimes_A P$ for finitely presented $A$-modules $P$ on finitely many locally closed strata. Identify $A_X$ with the completed coefficient sheaf $\varprojlim_n(A/\varpi^n)_X$ of [def-weil-pbc-adic-coefficient-datum] by the canonical isomorphism of [lem-weil-pbc-continuous-coefficients-immersion-restriction]. Let $D=D(\operatorname{Mod}(A_X))$ be the unbounded derived category [def-weil-abstract-derived-category] and let $K$ belong, under this identification, to the bounded constructible complete category [def-weil-pbc-bounded-constructible-complete]. For every small countable family $(M_i)_{i\in I}$ in $D$ with a common cohomological lower bound and every integer $q$, the canonical map of $A$-modules
$$\bigoplus_{i\in I}\operatorname{Hom}_D(K,M_i[q])\longrightarrow\operatorname{Hom}_D\bigl(K,(\bigoplus_{i\in I}M_i)[q]\bigr)$$
is an isomorphism. The map is induced by the shifted coprojections. The empty family is allowed; no assertion about families without a common lower bound is made.

source.place: Lemma 6.8.12; passage from global derived Hom to its cohomology, expanded using the shifted internal-Hom and K-injective interfaces.

proof.text: Put N_i=M_i[q] and shift the supplied colimiting cofan by q. The shift functor is an equivalence, so the new cofan is colimiting, and its common lower bound is n-q. Choose a coproduct of the G(N_i) in D(A), where G=adicGlobalRHom(K,-). Such coproducts exist by the termwise module coproduct construction and representatives. Apply integralConstructible_boundedBelow_compactness to N_i and the shifted cofan. Its canonical comparison is an isomorphism, so the cofan with legs G(iota_i[q]) is colimiting.

Apply derivedModuleHomology_coproduct in degree zero to that colimiting cofan. Forget the A-module structure and use the additive-group universe-lift functor to put the result in the universe of derived morphisms. Both functors preserve coproducts, so the resulting cofan of additive groups is colimiting. No bound on the global RHom outputs is needed.

On the pro-etale site, evaluation at the terminal object is naturally the group of maps from the unit sheaf: evaluate a unit map at 1, and extend a section at the terminal object to all objects by restriction. This identifies adicGlobalSections followed by forgetting scalars with the ordinary sections functor. The forgetful functor from modules to additive groups is exact; the standard composition comparison for right derived functors and its homology comparison therefore identify the underlying zeroth cohomology of adicDerivedGlobalSections with zeroth hypercohomology. Apply rhom_global_sectionsOfUniverses to the recorded internal Hom. This gives a natural additive isomorphism from the universe lift of H^0 G(N) to Hom(K,N). Only the additive comparison is needed: the final displayed map is already A-linear, and the module forgetful functor reflects colimits.

Transport the additive colimiting cofan through the natural isomorphism of the preceding step, using its components on every N_i and on the shifted coproduct point. Naturality says that its legs are postcomposition by iota_i[q]. Reflect this colimit along the forgetful functor from A-modules. Compare the resulting module colimit with the concrete direct-sum colimit: its unique comparison is definitionally the DirectSum.toModule map of the statement. The comparison of two colimits is an isomorphism, hence its underlying map is bijective. This argument applies unchanged to the empty family and to negative q.

lean.note: Uses the published PbcIntegralCategory specialization and its canonical ULift of the valuation ring. The ambient coproduct is an arbitrary colimiting cofan. DirectSum.toModule and Linear.rightComp give the actual coefficient-linear comparison induced by the shifted coprojections; bijectivity is precisely that this linear map is an isomorphism.
